Sources checked: Amazon's Creators API introduction page, Amazon Associates Program Policies, Amazon Conditions of Use (read 2 Oct), and claude/WYS_AUDIT_2026-10-02.md.

**Yes, the Creators API is built for software to use, not for gathering links by hand.** You don't log in and click around in it. A program sends it a request, like "search Amazon for pink dorm lamps" or "give me the details on these items", and gets product information back. So Claude using it to source products is the kind of use it's made for.

**What it can do.** Amazon lists four things:

- **SearchItems:** search products by keyword, filter or category.
- **GetItems:** pull details on specific products.
- **GetVariations:** get the sizes and colours of a product.
- **GetBrowseNodes:** look up Amazon's categories.

**The rules that matter for us, from Amazon's Program Policies:**

- **What it's for.** It can only be used for something whose main purpose is advertising and marketing Amazon. Every product you show has to link to its Amazon page. Pins and looks that link to your storefront or Idea Lists fit this.
- **Prices go stale fast.** Product info (other than images) can only be kept for 24 hours, then it has to be refreshed from the API. If prices are refreshed less often than hourly, they need a date and time shown next to them. Your pins already leave prices off, so this mostly doesn't affect you.
- **No saving Amazon's product photos.** Amazon's images can't be stored or copied, only linked to for up to 24 hours. That's fine for us, because your pins use original styling images, not Amazon's photos.
- **No AI training.** The data can't be used to train or fine-tune an AI model. Using Claude to search for products and pick some isn't training, so this rule doesn't block what we'd do.
- **Your key stays private.** Your API key is "for your personal use only" and can't be passed to anyone else. It would sit in your own connection, never shared.

**The one grey area.** Amazon also says that without its written approval, nobody may use the API for "aggregating, analyzing, extracting, or repurposing" product content. Searching for products to advertise them looks like normal use, since that's exactly what SearchItems is for. But Amazon's pages don't spell out AI assistants doing the searching. So I'd treat "Claude sources products for your own pins" as **likely allowed but not confirmed in writing**. The clean fix, once you're approved, is to email Associates support one question and keep their answer.

**What changes once you're approved.** Being eligible doesn't connect anything by itself. You'd generate your API key in Associates Central, then I'd set up and test a connection that lets Claude use it. Until that test passes, automatic sourcing stays UNVERIFIED, same as in the audit.

This matches claude/WYS_AUDIT_2026-10-02.md, which says eligibility alone doesn't prove a connection and keeps sourcing blocked until one is tested.

Sources:

- [Amazon Creators API – Introduction](https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/creatorsapi/docs/en-us/introduction)
- [Amazon Associates Program Policies](https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies)
- [Amazon Conditions of Use](https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088)
